claims.text: Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Heat treatment can invert this alloy from a continuous ordered B2 matrix to a continuous disordered BCC matrix containing discrete B2 precipitates.
The initially continuous ordered B2 matrix is brittle.
The as-solutionized alloy has a continuous ordered B2 matrix and brittle behavior.
A sequence of high-temperature solutionizing, rapid quenching, and prolonged low-temperature annealing produces the microstructural inversion.
Room-temperature and elevated-temperature uniaxial compression tests are applicable to this alloy.
The continuous ordered B2 phase facilitates cleavage fracture.
Replacing the ordered B2 matrix with a disordered BCC matrix increases dislocation mobility.
Discrete B2 precipitates strengthen the alloy through load transfer.
The inverted BCC-matrix/B2-precipitate microstructure restores ductility while retaining strengthening.
The proposed processing demonstrates a ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
The as-solutionized state is an intermediate brittle state reflecting temper embrittlement.
The continuous ordered B2 baseline has approximately 4-5% compressive fracture strain.
The continuous ordered B2 baseline exhibits cleavage-dominated fracture.
Excessive grain growth or undesirable secondary phases could irreversibly preserve brittleness.
Solutionizing the alloy can be used to produce a continuous brittle ordered B2 matrix.
Failure to obtain either microstructural inversion or recovered ductility would refute the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The specified trajectory begins with a brittle B2 state and ends with a more ductile BCC-matrix state, which establishes only a brittle-to-ductile transition. No preceding ductile state is specified to support the claimed ductile-brittle-ductile sequence.
The as-solutionized state is described both as the initial state and as an intermediate brittle state, leaving the ordering of the proposed transition internally ambiguous.
